title: Shared predicate constraints do not orient the current group/member projection
work_type: Manual selection correction; no new native experiment, corpus count, decoder or mathematical software.
question: Can a shared contrary, implication or other uniform predicate law select C1 versus its globally reversed L orientation?
answer: No, under the current positive-only projection with unassigned predicate extensions and no independent group/member facts. The two orientations are equisatisfiable even after any uniform pointwise Boolean constraint.

definitions.D_X: For every g in nonempty G, P_X({g},kappa)
definitions.Phi: The same condition on the full predicate truth vector at each nonempty argument S. It is independent of S identity/cardinality and does not relate different argument sets.
definitions.scope: Positive C_X/D_X requirements only. Predicate contents, participant groups and evaluation contexts remain unbound as in the recorded C1 projection.

manual_argument: For a singleton group, C_X and D_X coincide.
For a plural group in any satisfying interpretation, choose one old member a.
Give the new whole-group argument G the old full predicate vector on {a}. Give every new singleton argument {g} the old full predicate vector on G.
Every old positive D requirement holds at a, hence becomes a new positive C requirement. Every old positive C requirement is copied to every singleton, hence becomes a new positive D requirement.
Both copied vectors already satisfy the identical pointwise Phi. Other unmentioned arguments can retain allowed vectors. The same construction works in the opposite direction.

Separate paragraphs can be handled this way only while their group/member/context identities remain independently free; disjoint groups or contexts may then be chosen. The proof does not silently break a previously fixed shared identity.
essential_ceiling: This constructs another permitted interpretation of the unassigned predicate symbols. It is equal satisfiability, not equal truth in one fixed world and not permission to change an already bound lexical meaning or observed fact. It does not select any meaning or exclude collective/distributive language.
excluded_from_argument: Relations between group and member arguments
Fixed individual observations or referent overlaps
Events, ordered changes, results or frequencies
The currently unread remainder of either paragraph
